title: Early and late leaf spot disease on groundnuts

Header: Early and late leaf spot disease on groundnuts
Mycosphaerella (syn. Cercospora) arachidicola, Mycosphaerella berkeleyi (syn. Cercospora personata)

Prevention: Sow early, just before first rains, to reduce the severity of leaf spot disease.
For example, when groundnuts are followed by either maize or pasture, the disease development is slow and less severe.
Break for 3-4 years between successive bean crops.
Remove plant residues from field after harvest if the disease exists in your area, and bury deep in the soil.
Keep weeds under control because their heavy growth may encourage disease development.
Monitoring: Normal stages of attack are the vegetative, flowering and pod filling stages.
Look for the presence of leaf spots on the leaves, stems, petioles and pegs.
Disease, spots are similar in form and size to those of
Spot, but look out for spots that are darker brown on the underside of the leaflets and black on the upper side.
Look for spots that have less of a yellow ring or no ring at all.
Action should be taken immediately if 2 to 3 spots are observed on several plants per field.
Direct Control: If plants are clearly infected, remove and bury deep in the soil.
Note that burning is not allowed in many areas of
Chlorothalonil –based products (DIAMOND, BRAVO 720SC, CHLOROFLO 5OOSC, and others)
Copper oxy-chloride - based products (COPPER OXYCHLORIDE850g/l; CUPROZIN 35WP; and others).
Never spray more than 6 kg copper per ha per year !

Restrictions
When using a pesticide (even a botanical), always wear protective clothing.
Follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre- harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
Do not empty into drains.
WHO class
II pesticides might not be allowed in local
IPM schemes.
Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (ZEMA).
WHO toxicity class
U, unlikely hazardous when used as per product instructions; pre-harvest interval (p.h.i.) 7 days; restricted re-entry interval (r.e.i.) 1 day after spray.
Max 2 sprays per season at 0.2% (1.5lts/ha) chlorothalonil after the emergence of the infection, at intervals of 10 - 15 days starting 40 days after germination up to 90 days.
This provides effective control to early and late leaf spots.
Do not use near water sources.
WHO class
II (moderately hazardous); p.h.i. 14 days, r.e.i. 3 days.
Usually applied at 40-80 mg per 20 litres and, 2-4kg per hectare, but double-check with product label.
When used too much, copper(II)-ions can accumulate in soil and water.
It can burn leaves.
Do not use during fruit set.
